title: Downloaded pptx and pdf docs are not valid files
description: the downloaded pptx and pdf docs are not valid files
cause: When binary assets (PPTX/PDF) or Google Workspace documents (Docs, Slides, Sheets) are retrieved from Google Drive via direct GET/raw content stream rather than Google Drive API's dedicated export endpoints (/files/{id}/export?mimeType=application/pdf or PPTX MIME type), or when binary responses are decoded/written as UTF-8 text rather than raw binary bytes, file headers (e.g. %PDF or PPTX zip magic numbers) are corrupted, rendering the downloaded files invalid and unopenable.
proposed_plan:
1. Update server.py download endpoint and client download handlers to distinguish between binary Drive files and native Google Workspace files.
2. For Google Slides/Docs, route requests to the Drive export API with explicit MIME types (application/pdf for PDF, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation for PPTX).
3. Ensure all binary downloads are streamed and written in binary mode ('wb') with proper Content-Type and Content-Disposition headers.

title: Issue/Risk Name does not appear - only the description is shown
description: the issue/risk name doesnt appear - only the description
cause: In the CSV parsing logic (googleSheetsService.ts), mock data generation (mockData.ts), and table rendering columns (WholeDataTab.tsx, IssueRegisterView.tsx), column mapping was shifted by several columns. For issues, issueOwner was loaded with the issue title while issueName was loaded with the Action Plan/Schedule; for risks, riskName was populated with the Category name ('Legal/Contract', 'Scope', 'Schedule') while the actual Risk Title resided in riskOwner or bundle. As a result, the true title/name was obscured and only descriptions or categories appeared.
proposed_plan:
1. Correct column mappings in googleSheetsService.ts and ImportDataModal.tsx to match Google Sheet headers: map 'Risk Title' / 'Risk Name' / 'Issue Title' directly to riskName / issueName, map 'Owner' to riskOwner / issueOwner, 'Category' to causeCategory, and 'Description' to riskDescription / issueDescription.
2. Update mockData.ts and table column renderers in WholeDataTab.tsx, RiskMatrix.tsx, CD1DriverTree.tsx, and IssueRegisterView.tsx to consistently display the resolved Name/Title prominently alongside the description.

title: Risk numbers are rendered as R-008 instead of matching sheet format (8)
description: risk numbers are rendered as R-008 not matching the sheet (8)
cause: In googleSheetsService.ts, ImportDataModal.tsx, App.tsx, and mockData.ts, risk IDs are forcibly transformed with zero-padded prefixes (RSK-008 or R-008) rather than preserving the raw integer format (8) used in the source Google Sheet. This causes a format mismatch with the spreadsheet, prevents natural numerical sorting, and breaks cross-referencing between related issues (which reference plain IDs like '15', '20', '24').
proposed_plan:
1. Refactor ID ingestion and display logic in googleSheetsService.ts, types.ts, WholeDataTab.tsx, and RiskMatrix.tsx to support and prioritize integer display formatting (e.g. displayId: '8' or stripping non-essential prefixes where integer IDs exist), while maintaining backward compatibility for prefixed IDs.
2. Ensure search, matrix badges, table ID columns, and related risk links display '8' (matching the sheet) instead of 'R-008'/'RSK-008'.
